suite.title: Graphics quality and subjective experience in a WebXR room

study.title: Graphics quality and subjective experience in a WebXR room
study.researchQuestion: RQ1: How does the graphics quality of a virtual environment (low, medium, high) affect presence, perceived realism, visual appeal, visual discomfort, preference and a material-search task?
study.agentQuestions: RQ2: Which agent methods (text only, reading the project files, using the app, adding an evidence document, knowing the participants) reproduce these human differences?

conditions.label: High quality (PBR materials, reflections, soft shadows)

cases.label: Main: Select the glossy ceramic mug, the brushed-metal bowl and the glass vase.
Main: Select the glossy ceramic mug, the brushed-metal bowl and the glass vase.

sources.label: Study brief
sources.description: examples/graphics-quality/agent-brief.md: room, task, the three quality levels and the questionnaire items, without any participant answers.

sources.label: WebXR project
sources.description: examples/graphics-quality/webxr-app/: the scene, the material settings per quality level and the task logic. Run it with ?quality=low|medium|high&study=1.

sources.label: Toy evidence note
sources.description: examples/graphics-quality/evidence/toy-evidence.md: invented, general statements about visual fidelity and experience. Not fitted to the synthetic answers.

sources.label: Participant demographics
sources.description: data/raw/demographics.csv, cohort summary only for population forecasts.

outcomes.label: Search time
outcomes.description: Geometric mean over the four scored main trials; practice excluded.

outcomes.label: Wrong selections
outcomes.description: Mean number of non-target objects selected per scored main trial.

outcomes.label: Presence (4 items)
outcomes.description: Mean of four presence items (general, spatial, involvement, realness), asked after each level.

outcomes.label: Perceived realism
outcomes.description: 'How realistic did the objects and room look?' after each level.

outcomes.label: Visual appeal
outcomes.description: 'How visually appealing was the scene?' after each level.

outcomes.label: Visual discomfort
outcomes.description: 'How much visual discomfort (eye strain, blur, flicker) did you feel?' after each level.

outcomes.label: Overall preference
outcomes.description: Final ranking of the three levels after the whole session.

notes: Built-in deterministic analyzer using the embedded study outcomes, family weights, tie tolerance, bootstrap draws and seed.
Contrasts may be added by later continuations; they do not change the scoring definition of existing outcomes.
Each condition is one agent protocol. Continuations may add models, protocols and repetitions; unchanged jobs are reused.
